name: Ḥunayn’s medical translation network
description: Ḥunayn ibn Isḥāq and associates translated Greek medical texts into Syriac and Arabic; a dated epistle records work including Galen’s Method of Healing to Glaucon.

date.basis: The cited account provides this period, not an exact date.

events.statement: Ḥunayn prepared an epistle to his patron identifying Galen translations, including an Arabic Method of Healing to Glaucon described as recently finished.

evidence.supports: Describes Hunayn’s Greek-to-Syriac-to-Arabic translation network, identifies the Arabic Method of Healing to Glaucon as finished around the epistle’s first version, and explains dating uncertainties.
Dates the first version of Hunayn’s epistle to 855–856 from a note in the text, identifies sponsor Ali ibn Yahya ibn al-Munajjim and notes later revisions.

contributions.resource: Authored the epistle and worked on medical translations.

evidence.supports: Describes Hunayn’s Greek-to-Syriac-to-Arabic translation network, identifies the Arabic Method of Healing to Glaucon as finished around the epistle’s first version, and explains dating uncertainties.
Dates the first version of Hunayn’s epistle to 855–856 from a note in the text, identifies sponsor Ali ibn Yahya ibn al-Munajjim and notes later revisions.

events.scope: The 855–856 date applies to the first epistle version, not to every translation it surveys; the timing of the Glaucon translation is inferred from the phrase “in these days”.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest scoped episode established in these sources; not a global priority claim.

caveats: A later redacted epistle and scholarly interpretations witness prior translation activity. The exact dates and collaborators of individual translations are generally uncertain; the translation of Method of Healing to Glaucon is inferred as approximately contemporary, not precisely dated. Patronage of the epistle does not prove who paid for each translation. Translation did not require a single institutional House of Wisdom.

research.note: Independent review checked the 855–856 epistle and the qualified inference about the Glaucon translation in the searchable passages of Vagelpohl’s article; the other cited PDF was blocked.
